Habermas’s distinction is not captured by either of the two options given: “law as medium” means law functioning as a steering mechanism for social subsystems (e.g., economy, administration), while “law as institution” means law as a normative framework embedded in the lifeworld that secures democratic legitimacy and shared values. Therefore, neither “media vs. courts” nor “statutes vs. police/executive” accurately describes the distinction.  
CONFIDENCE: 92
